fields.questionText: A circle with centre O has radius 6 cm. From an external point P, two tangents PA and PB are drawn to the circle such that the tangents are perpendicular to each other. Find OP and the length of each tangent, and verify your answer.
solutionSteps: Since ∠APB = 90° and OP bisects ∠APB, ∠OPA = 45°; also OA ⊥ PA (radius ⊥ tangent), so triangle OAP is right-angled at A.
sin 45° = OA/OP ⇒ OP = 6/sin 45° = 6√2 cm.
Tangent length PA = OP × cos 45° = 6√2 × (1/√2) = 6 cm (so PB = 6 cm too).
Verification: OA² + PA² = 36 + 36 = 72 = (6√2)² = OP². ✓
fields.finalAnswer: OP = 6√2 cm; each tangent length = 6 cm.

fields.questionText: A seedling is kept in a box that has a single opening on one side through which light enters. After a few days, its shoot is seen bending and growing towards the opening. Identify the stimulus that causes the shoot to grow in this direction.
options: Gravity
Light
Water
Touch
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Correct option: Light. The shoot bends towards the opening through which light enters — this is positive phototropism, so the stimulus is light.

fields.questionText: A potted plant is kept near a window. After a few days its shoot is seen bending towards the light coming in through the window. Explain how the plant hormone controls this growth response of the shoot.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] The hormone auxin is synthesised at the shoot tip and diffuses down the shoot.
[1 mark] When light falls from one side, auxin collects on the side of the shoot away from the light (the shaded side).
[1 mark] Auxin causes the cells on the shaded side to elongate more, so that side grows faster and the shoot bends towards the light (phototropism).

fields.questionText:
Attempt either (a) or (b).
(a) "The timing and the amount of hormone secreted by a gland are regulated in the human body." Justify this statement with the help of an example.
OR
(b) Electrical impulse is an excellent means to transmit information in the animal body, but there are some limitations to the use of electrical impulses. State any two limitations.
fields.answer: (a) The timing and amount of hormone released are regulated by a feedback mechanism. Example: when blood sugar level rises, it is detected by cells of the pancreas, which secrete more insulin; as blood sugar falls, insulin secretion is reduced. (Any other suitable example.) OR (b) (1) Electrical impulses reach only those cells that are connected by nervous tissue, not each and every cell of the body. (2) Once a cell generates and transmits an impulse, it takes time to reset its mechanism before it can generate a new impulse, so cells cannot continually create and transmit impulses.
solutionSteps: (a) The timing and amount of hormone released are regulated by a feedback mechanism.
(a) Example: when blood sugar level rises, the pancreas cells detect it and secrete more insulin; as blood sugar falls, insulin secretion is reduced. (Any other suitable example.)
OR (b) Limitation 1: Electrical impulses reach only those cells that are connected by nervous tissue, not each and every cell in the body.
(b) Limitation 2: After generating and transmitting an impulse, a cell takes time to reset its mechanism before it can transmit a new one, so transmission is not continuous.
fields.finalAnswer: (a) Feedback mechanism — e.g. rise in blood sugar → more insulin from pancreas; fall → less insulin. OR (b) Impulses reach only cells connected by nervous tissue; cells need time to reset before a new impulse, so transmission is not continuous.

rationale: Removed stray mark '2' and laid out the internal choice; answer/finalAnswer previously omitted part (a) — now give both alternatives.

fields.questionText: In a reflex arc, a bee sting causes the arm to be moved quickly. In this arc, P is the sensory neurone, Q is the relay neurone and R is the motor neurone. If the relay neurone Q is damaged, how will the transmission of nerve impulses in the reflex arc be affected?
options: Impulses cannot pass from P → Q
Impulses cannot pass from P → R
Impulses cannot pass from Q → P
Impulses cannot pass from R → Q
fields.answer: Impulses cannot pass from P → R
solutionSteps: Correct option is (b) Impulses cannot pass from P → R.
P is the sensory neurone, Q is the relay neurone and R is the motor neurone. The impulse travels P → Q → R; if Q is damaged, the impulse from the sensory neurone P cannot reach the motor neurone R.
fields.finalAnswer: (b) Impulses cannot pass from P → R

fields.questionText: Adrenaline hormone is secreted in the body during emergency situations. What would be the effect of an increased concentration of adrenaline on (I) the concentration of glycogen in the liver and (II) the concentration of glucose in the blood?
options: (I) Decrease; (II) Increase
(I) Increase; (II) Increase
(I) No effect; (II) Decrease
(I) Increase; (II) No effect
solutionSteps: Correct option is (a): glycogen in the liver decreases; glucose in the blood increases.
Adrenaline is secreted during the fight-or-flight response. It increases the breakdown of glycogen to glucose in the liver and muscles, so liver glycogen falls and blood glucose rises.

solutionSteps: [1 mark] (a) It is a reflex action; the pathway involved is the reflex arc.
[1 mark] (b) Stimulus (heat) → Receptor (skin) → Sensory neurone → Spinal cord (relay neurone) → Motor neurone → Effector (arm muscles) → hand is withdrawn.
[1 mark] (c) It is faster because the impulse is processed in the spinal cord and does not have to travel to the brain for thinking/decision.
[1 mark] (d) The response is coordinated by the spinal cord (central nervous system).
fields.finalAnswer: (a) Reflex action via reflex arc; (b) Receptor → Sensory neurone → Spinal cord → Motor neurone → Effector; (c) processed in spinal cord, no brain involvement; (d) Spinal cord.
